Full-metric benchmark of RepeatMasker on simulated genomes, complete vs. incomplete library

Ting-Hsuan Chen

05 November, 2026

  • 1. Base-pair-level metrics (TEbenchtop mode 2)
  • 2. False positives
  • 3. Recall by identity and integrity (TEbenchtop mode 2 slices)
  • 4. Locus-level evaluation (TEbenchtop mode 3)
  • 5. Notes

Revision items 23-28 (R2#5, R3-major#6, #7, #12, R3-minor#10, #16). RepeatMasker annotations of the five scenario 1 genomes (Fig. 3D) are scored against the simulator’s ground-truth GFF with TEbenchtop (15_tair10_benchmark_repeatmasker.sh):

  • mode 2: base-pair-level TP/FP/FN, recall (sensitivity), precision, F1 and FDR, overall and by TE type, and per identity x integrity slice;
  • mode 3: per-locus overlaps with the annotation (boundaries, coverage, number of hits).

Three libraries are compared: the complete library used for simulation (full), and the same library with 25% or 50% of families removed at random (drop25, drop50; drop50 removes all of drop25’s families plus as many again). Removing families mimics annotating a genome whose library lacks some families, as for non-model organisms. The evaluation only needs the annotation as a GFF, so the same workflow applies to any annotation tool, including de novo pipelines.

2. False positives

False-positive loci are RepeatMasker hits that overlap no simulated TE. Because mode 1 inserts TEs into the TE-depleted TAIR10 genome, some of these hits may be TE remnants left in the backbone after masking rather than annotation errors; RepeatMasker on the backbone alone (full library) measures that baseline.

False-positive loci (hits overlapping no simulated TE) and false-positive bases (mean and SD of 5 replicates).

4. Locus-level evaluation (TEbenchtop mode 3)

For every simulated locus, the RepeatMasker hit with the largest overlap (either strand) is used for classification; same-strand hits are used for boundaries and fragmentation.

  • Fragmentation: number of same-strand RepeatMasker hits covering the locus (0 = missed, 1 = single hit, >= 2 = split into several hits).
  • Merging: a RepeatMasker hit overlapping two or more simulated loci.
  • Boundary accuracy: start/end difference (bp) between a locus and its single same-strand hit.
  • Classification: the best hit’s family, superfamily and class compared with the simulated locus. Loci whose family was removed from the library are reported separately: they can only be annotated with a related family, or missed.

4.3 Classification by superfamily

Ribbon plots and bar plots adapted from 31.02_BM_TEtrimmer.Rmd. Each simulated locus is counted once, using its best-overlapping hit (loci with no hit are shown as “not detected”); counts are the mean per replicate. RepeatMasker labels hits with the library’s own classification, which is the one used by the simulator, so no renaming of superfamilies is needed.

Saved file name: bm_classification_ribbon_all.png

Loci of the removed families only (drop25 and drop50): these can only be annotated with a related family, or missed.

5. Notes

  • Nested insertions (R3-minor#16, item 28) are analysed in 24.1_item34_35_nesting_beta_sensitivity.Rmd.
  • Base-pair-level metrics do not depend on an overlap threshold; the reciprocal-overlap threshold check (item 26) is a separate analysis.
  • Removed families are the same in every replicate (one fixed random order), so differences between replicates reflect the simulated genomes, not the choice of families.
